flags.reason: The guide gives no accessibility guidance; left empty rather than guessed.

summary: Add a subordinate signal to a main item without altering its footprint.

useWhen.text: Add a subordinate signal to a main item without altering its footprint.

from.quote: Add a subordinate signal to a main item without altering its footprint.

useWhen.text: Keep a small qualifier, such as a payment type or status, attached to the item it describes.

from.quote: The badge adds a small qualification such as payment type or status while the central mark remains easy to recognize.

avoidWhen.text: The extra signal is the item's primary label or would become a second focal point: the badge stays subordinate to the main item.

from.quote: The badge should not carry the primary label or become a second focal point.

anatomy.holds: The child in the main slot (children): it establishes the size and is the visual object people identify first.

from.quote: The child in the main slot establishes the size and the visual object people identify first.

anatomy.holds: The badge slot: centred on the selected anchor, so it can straddle the main edge.

from.quote: The badge slot is centered on the selected anchor and can straddle the main edge.

anatomy.holds: Position chooses one of nine anchors; the token ring around the badge separates the compact signal from the main mark.

from.quote: Position chooses one of nine anchors; the token ring separates a compact signal from the main mark.

placementAdvice.text: The main child owns its size and Attached does not grow the layout footprint for the badge, so give its host enough whitespace for the overhang.

from.quote: Attached does not grow the layout footprint for the badge, so its host needs enough whitespace for the overhang.

placementAdvice.text: Leave slack around the composition so the badge can straddle the edge.

from.quote: Leave slack around the composition so the badge can straddle the edge.

placementAdvice.text: Do not clip the host with overflow hidden: the badge overhangs the main bounds and is visibly cut off.

from.quote: Overflow hidden turns a positioning choice into a visibly cut-off signal.

placementAdvice.text: Keep the qualifier next to the item it describes, as in a payment row.

from.quote: A payment row keeps the qualifier next to the item it describes.

configuration.text: Use the position choices for where the badge belongs.

from.quote: Use the exposed position choices for where the badge belongs.

configuration.text: Use an edge or corner anchor when the badge describes the item.

from.quote: Use edge or corner anchors when the badge describes the item.

configuration.text: Avoid the center anchor unless the overlay is deliberate: a centred badge covers the main mark.

from.quote: A center anchor is reserved for a deliberate overlay.

configuration.text: For a diagonal (corner) anchor, choose whether it sits on the round child’s edge or on its bounding-box corner.

from.quote: For diagonal anchors, choose the round child’s edge or its bounding-box corner.

configuration.text: Circle edge, circular true (the default), for round marks such as a circular IconCapsule: corner anchors sit on the circle.

from.quote: use Circle edge for round marks and Bounding box for a square corner relationship.

configuration.text: Bounding box, circular false, for a square corner relationship: corner anchors sit on the bounding-box corners.

from.quote: use Circle edge for round marks and Bounding box for a square corner relationship.

configuration.text: Size IconCapsule children with their Icon Capsule Size modes, not style dimensions, so they keep their circular geometry: the guide uses M for the main item and XS for the badge.

from.quote: this guide uses the native Icon Capsule Size modes M and XS so both child capsules keep their component-owned circular geometry.

rules.text: Let the attachment support the item, not obscure it.

from.quote: Attachment supports the item, never obscures it.

rules.text: Use a compact, meaningful signal that clarifies the main item.

from.quote: Use a compact, meaningful signal that clarifies the main item.

rules.text: Make the main item readable first: the badge adds a small qualification, such as payment type or status, while the central mark stays easy to recognise.

from.quote: The badge adds a small qualification such as payment type or status while the central mark remains easy to recognize.

rules.text: Choose a familiar icon or small signal that people can understand at a glance.

from.quote: Choose a familiar icon or small signal that people can understand at a glance.

rules.text: Do not make the badge compete with the main item: an oversized attachment pulls focus away from it.

from.quote: An oversized attachment pulls focus away from the main item.

examples.purpose: The guide's composition: a main IconCapsule at its default size with a compact IconCapsule badge (Icon Capsule Size XS) on the default bottom-right anchor, projected onto the circle's edge.
examples.jsx:
<Attached badge={<IconCapsule iconName="ic_rupee" modes={{ 'Icon Capsule Size': 'XS' }} />}>
  <IconCapsule iconName="ic_cart" />
</Attached>

from.quote: this guide uses the native Icon Capsule Size modes M and XS so both child capsules keep their component-owned circular geometry.

props.name: children
props.description: Main content the badge attaches to (the Figma "main slot"). Any node — typically an `IconCapsule`, `Avatar`, image, etc. `modes` are cascaded to every child via {@link cloneChildrenWithModes}.

props.name: badge
props.description: The element attached on top of `children` (the Figma "slot"). Centered on the anchor point given by `position` so it straddles the edge/corner. `modes` are cascaded into it as well.

props.name: badgeSize
props.description: Enforces a fixed square size (in px) on the `badge` slot, regardless of what node is passed. The badge is wrapped in a box of `badgeSize × badgeSize` with `overflow: 'hidden'`, and the badge content is stretched to fill it. Use this to guarantee the design-token size even when a consumer drops in an arbitrary node (e.g. an `Image`) whose intrinsic size/aspect-ratio would otherwise win. When omitted, the badge keeps its own intrinsic size (legacy behavior).

props.name: badgeRadius
props.description: Corner radius used to clip the `badge` box. Only applies when `badgeSize` is set. Anything that overflows the rounded box (e.g. a non-square image) is clipped.

props.name: position
props.description: Anchor point for the `badge` relative to the main content. Default "bottom-right", from the component source.

props.name: circular
props.description: How the anchor point is computed for diagonal (corner) positions: - `true` (default): treat the main content as a **circle** inscribed in its bounding box — corner anchors sit on the circle's circumference (the 45° point), so badges hug round content like a circular `IconCapsule` or `Avatar`. - `false`: treat the main content as a **square** — corner anchors sit on the bounding-box corners. Edge (`top`/`bottom`/`left`/`right`) and `center` anchors are unaffected, since the circle meets the bounding box at those points. Default true, from the component source.

props.name: modes
props.description: Mode configuration cascaded to the token resolver and all children.

props.name: ...Omit<ViewProps, 'children'>
props.description: Inherited React Native props the component also accepts. They are not part of the design contract and no guide documents them.

modes.name: Attached Border
modes.description: A token collection Attached reads (the package's FIGMA_COMPONENT_MODES). When modes leave it unset, the resolver uses the collection's default mode.

modes.name: Color Mode
modes.description: A token collection Attached reads (the package's FIGMA_COMPONENT_MODES). When modes leave it unset, the resolver uses the collection's default mode.
